title: When a competitor strikes, size the threat in revenue terms and compare every response with doing nothing
description: The first question to ask in a competitive response case, how to structure it, and the trap to avoid.
hook: When a rival makes a move, the client wants to know how to respond. Here is how to keep your head and give a balanced answer.
body:
The first question to ask

How big is the threat in revenue terms?

How to build your structure

  • Exposure (customers, revenue and margin at risk)
  • Rival's motive (segments targeted, can they keep it up)
  • Options (do nothing, defend current customers, respond on price or product, partner or buy)
  • Choose on impact, cost, speed and risk vs doing nothing

The trap most people fall into

Not comparing to doing nothing.

For the full tree, with every branch, read the competitive response framework.

Two prompts to try

A rival has cut prices 20% on our best-selling product. How do we respond?

Show a model structure
  • The threat: What exactly did they cut, where, for how long?; Their costs: can they sustain it?
  • Impact on us: Customers lost so far and at risk; Profit at risk under each scenario
  • Our options: Match, partly match, hold, differentiate; Target only the customers at risk
  • Their likely reaction: Price war risk; How long they can keep it up vs us

Where to start: Impact first: how many customers actually switch before we react.

The trap: Matching the price immediately without sizing what is really at risk.
outro: Small things like this add up. Try it in your next practice case and notice how it changes the conversation. Practise this case type in the free casebook: every case has a worked answer.
